x: The season progressed through county, district and AAA Championships which were highlighted by a magnificent win by Sydney Wooderson, who despite a lapse of five years and army service, moved up to a new distance and broke the British 3 mile record, defeating the formidable Willie Slykhuis of Holland in the process.
Other titles to go abroad were the 3 miles won by Wooderson's old rival Willie Slykhuis, the Dutch star, and the High and Long jumps to visiting Australian Olympians.
My ignorance soon became apparent when Sydney Wooderson became the first Briton to break 14 minutes for the distance, closely followed by the flying Dutchman Willie Slykhuis.
